subject: gov.policy
name: Data Centre and Cloud Computing Services Regulations 2025
milestone: Full text held from 2026-09-02; listed as current in the regulator's catalogue
position_end: Named by the regulator as current and now held in full, with licence categories distinguishing operators owning data centres inside Sudan from renters and cloud resellers

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Transformation Authority
milestone: Established by PM decree, alongside the Sudanese Data and AI Authority and the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority
position_end: Established; institutional scaffolding predates any of the platform-level claims that follow it; e-government development index 0.2759 (2024, below the 0.4247 African average) cited alongside
sources: 2025-11-07 Sudan Establishes Three Digital Authorities to Advance E-Govt|2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026
note: No account held connects this institutional decree to the platform claims that follow it

subject: gov.policy
name: E-Government and Smart Transition Plan 2016-2020
milestone: Covered 2016 to 2020
position_end: Expired in 2020; the plan's own text could not be captured
note: Held on title and citation evidence only; the document itself did not fetch

subject: gov.policy
name: Hosting-location disclosure in telecommunications licensing
milestone: Required under the Licensing Regulation for the Telecommunications and Postal Sector 2019
position_end: Applicants for an internet-applications licence must disclose whether their hosting server sits inside or outside Sudan, and which company hosts it
note: No economy-wide data-localisation law is held; this sectoral requirement is the closest instrument

subject: gov.policy
name: Knowledge Society strategy 2007-2011
milestone: Approved 2007 under the twenty-five-year national strategy; ran to 2011
position_end: Expired in 2011 with no successor located; implementation was rated good at the time

subject: gov.legislate
name: Banking Agency Licensing Regulation 2026
milestone: Issued 1 March 2026 under the Banking Business Organisation Act 2004
position_end: In force, letting banks deliver cash, transfer and bill-payment services through licensed agents outside branches, subject to transaction ceilings and anti-money-laundering compliance

subject: gov.legislate
name: Border-trade legal framework (state-level protocols)
milestone: Meeting chaired by the finance minister resolved to review state-to-neighbouring-country trade protocols and refer them to the Council of Ministers, to build a single national legal framework in their place
position_end: Resolution passed to review and unify state-level agreements; no transition arrangement, timetable or affected-protocol list given
note: Paired with Baladna's adoption as sole foreign-trade platform; stated driver is revenue protection, not service delivery

subject: gov.legislate
name: Central bank circular 7/2026 on USSD financial services
milestone: Issued 31 March 2026
position_end: In force, requiring fee disclosure, no debit on failed transactions, transaction notifications, a round-the-clock complaint centre, 48-hour resolution, and encryption to TLS 1.2 and ISO/IEC 27001

subject: gov.legislate
name: Central bank circular 8/2026 on anti-money-laundering controls for payment channels
milestone: Issued 30 April 2026
position_end: In force, extending monitoring, exception reporting, funding and value limits and service suspension to mobile and phone payment channels

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cyber Crime Prevention (Amendment) Act 2020
milestone: Signed 22 April 2020, gazetted 13 July 2020
position_end: In force, sharply increasing penalties across articles 5 to 39 of the 2018 Cyber Crime Law
note: Not AI-specific; no dedicated deepfake or generative-AI provision is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrime law prosecutions for speech
milestone: Six-year sentence over a private phone conversation, reported 2026-08-17
position_end: A pharmacist sentenced to six years over a private phone conversation opposing the war, convicted under the 1991 criminal code and the cybercrime law after intelligence officers searched his phone, and a journalist detained on a cybercrime complaint filed by an intelligence officer and held without questioning
note: the two accounts date the cybercrime statute differently, to 2007 and to 2008; neither judgment nor charging instrument is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Draft Digital Transformation Law of 2026
milestone: Redrafting with the digital transformation ministry reported 2026-08-11
position_end: No text published. The justice ministry states it is preparing the instrument in coordination with the digital transformation and communications ministry, as the Digital Transformation Regulation Law of 2026
note: Third of the three-instrument package

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Transactions Act 2007
milestone: In force since 2007; named as the legal basis for the national digital identity in 2026
position_end: In force, covering digital signatures, electronic authentication and certification, and cited as the operative basis for SUDAPASS
note: A consolidated text of the 2015 amendment was not located

subject: gov.legislate
name: Mobile Payment Financial Institutions Licensing Regulation 2020
milestone: Approved by the central bank's board on 28 December 2020
position_end: In force, setting licensing conditions, capital and insurance requirements, e-money and trust-account rules, agent rules and consumer-protection duties

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act 2003
milestone: Assessed in 2021 as not providing for recent advances in statistical production
position_end: In force and assessed as outdated, with no gender-statistics provisions; the full primary text is not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Telecommunications and Post (Organization) Act 2018
milestone: Repealed the 1910 Post and Telegraphs Act and the 2001 Communications Act
position_end: In force, constituting the telecommunications and post regulator and carrying the postal-addressing mandate the regulator states as its duty

subject: gov.protect
name: Bank customer data-update directive
milestone: Deadline extended to end-2026 on 2026-08-17
position_start: Banks ordered on 2026-08-12 to suspend and freeze customer accounts not updated by 30 September 2026, under anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing data-verification and transaction-monitoring requirements
position_end: The deadline extended to the end of 2026, with the national digital identity system's rollout named as the route by which customers are to update their data; bankers back the directive as necessary for the banking system's soundness while warning that freezing non-compliant accounts risks financial exclusion amid war-driven displacement and lost documentation
note: the directive text is not held; no count of accounts affected, no exception for displaced customers without documents and no appeal route is stated

subject: gov.protect
name: Draft Data and Artificial Intelligence Law
milestone: Redrafting with the digital transformation ministry reported 2026-08-11
position_end: No statute in force and no published text. The justice ministry states it is preparing the instrument in coordination with the digital transformation and communications ministry, as the Data and Artificial Intelligence Regulation Law of 2026
note: Legislating data protection and AI in one instrument is a design few African states have attempted

subject: gov.regional
name: IGAD cybersecurity legal-framework harmonisation
milestone: Consultancy awarded, disclosed 30 December 2025
position_start: Terms of reference issued, no consultant appointed
position_end: A USD 336,700 consultancy awarded to harmonise cybersecurity legal frameworks across IGAD member states

subject: gov.regional
name: IGAD regional guidelines on data hosting and the cloud market
milestone: Expressions of interest invited 30 March 2026
position_end: At procurement stage: a consultancy invited to develop harmonised regional guidelines for infrastructure sharing, co-location, data hosting and the cloud market

subject: gov.regional
name: ITU resolution on rebuilding Sudan's telecommunications infrastructure
milestone: Adopted by consensus at the World Telecommunication Development Conference, 26 November 2025
position_end: Adopted, creating a formal basis for international technical and financial assistance to rebuild war-damaged telecommunications infrastructure

subject: gov.regional
name: Port Sudan to Douala fibre corridor (Sudan section)
milestone: At pre-feasibility stage in the continental infrastructure programme
position_end: Planned, positioning Sudan as a transit route linking Chad, the Central African Republic, Ethiopia and South Sudan with open-access gateways

subject: gov.standards
name: Country signing certificate in the ICAO Public Key Directory
milestone: Deposited in Montreal, announced 15 February 2026
position_end: Deposited, enabling worldwide verification of Sudan's machine-readable passports under the ICAO Doc 9303 trust chain

subject: gov.standards
name: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
milestone: Issued January 2026 over the central bank governor's signature
position_end: Mandatory for banks and financial institutions, requiring alignment with ISO 27001, ISO 27002, NIST, ISF, Basel and PCI DSS

subject: gov.standards
name: Electronic payment of standards-certification fees
milestone: Launched in Khartoum, 26 July 2026
position_end: Certification fees payable through the national collection service integrated with the government platform

subject: gov.standards
name: National technical standards or interoperability framework
milestone: Standards catalogue published under the Standards Act 2008
position_end: A national standards body publishing adopted Sudanese Standards against their ISO equivalents, and a government-platform product naming interoperability as a design principle
note: No whole-of-government interoperability framework is held; the 2016-2020 e-government plan has expired

subject: gov.standards
name: Telecommunications Service Quality Regulation 2026
milestone: Gazetted 15 March 2026, repealing the 2021 regulation
position_end: In force, made under the Telecommunications and Post Regulation Act 2018 with the minister's approval
note: Substantive quality and performance provisions from page 7 onwards are not held

subject: gov.discourse
name: Private Sector Engagement Strategy 2026-2028
milestone: Published 29 April 2026 on 71 key-informant interviews
position_end: Published, built on interviews with small firms, banks, business associations, displaced firms and diaspora businesses, and shaping recovery priorities that include telecommunications

subject: gov.discourse
name: Zain Interactive Forum
milestone: Seventh edition held 31 May 2026
position_end: A private-sector-hosted forum whose seventh edition called for a national artificial-intelligence and digital-transformation strategy and a supreme council for digital transformation

subject: finance.budget
name: Treasury Single Account (TSA) implementation
milestone: State minister of finance reaffirmed commitment to implementing the TSA system, at the African Summit for Social Impact (Abuja)
position_end: Commitment reaffirmed; no target date, phase or coverage given

subject: finance.mou
name: YahClick and Canar satellite-broadband partnership
milestone: Six-year agreement signed 23 January 2023
position_end: A USD 15 million six-year satellite-broadband partnership with a Sudanese operator, framed against digital-transformation and e-government goals

subject: finance.new
name: ASCENT-Sudan energy and digital access operation
milestone: Effective 25 October 2025; telecom-energy request for proposals launched 1 April 2026
position_end: Effective, with over 30 private-sector expressions of interest received and two requests for proposals launched; the targets of 150,000 people with new internet access and 50 telecom sites with improved energy stood at nil in March 2026
note: The World Bank's own project record still showed the operation at pipeline status when checked, so no deal record was built

subject: finance.new
name: Khartoum Stock Exchange online-trading system (AfDB PFM project)
milestone: Online trading launched on the Khartoum Stock Exchange, financed by the African Development Bank (reported US$34.8m) under its Public Financial and Macroeconomic Management project
position_end: Launched 2016-03-24; no later report on file updates it
note: A decade predates, and is not referenced by, the 2026 PFM directives that restate the same payroll/e-invoicing/e-procurement list

subject: finance.new
name: Primary Education Emergency Support Project
milestone: Board approval 19 November 2024; expected closing 31 December 2026
position_end: A USD 41.9 million grant covering offline learning servers, tablets, solar power, digital learning hubs and dashboard-based monitoring in reopened primary schools

subject: infra.connect
name: 4G tower expansion programme
milestone: Digital ministry reports 60 4G towers built, with 200 more planned during 2026
position_end: 60 towers built; 200 more planned for 2026
note: No later source confirms progress against the 200-tower target

subject: infra.connect
name: Exam-period internet shutdowns
milestone: Shutdowns imposed 13 to 15 April 2026
position_start: Shutdowns imposed in each prior exam season
position_end: Imposed again for the sixth consecutive year, with one satellite provider growing to 27 per cent of the internet-service market as terrestrial usage collapsed during the suspensions

subject: infra.connect
name: Horizon Fiber Initiative (Djibouti-Ethiopia-Sudan corridor)
milestone: Tripartite binding agreement signed in Djibouti, converting the Dec-2024 MoU
position_end: Binding tripartite agreement; ~2,800km corridor, 144 fibre pairs, ~14ms target latency, linking Djibouti subsea landings via Ethiopia to Port Sudan, interconnecting with the existing Port Sudan-Jeddah cable
note: Physical build/completion date not stated in any source held

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet users
milestone: Measured at October 2025
position_end: 14.9 million users, 28.7 per cent of the population (October 2025), up 407,000 or 2.8 per cent year on year with penetration unchanged
note: The World Bank and ITU series for Sudan carries no observation after 18.6 per cent for 2017

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile internet bundle prices
milestone: Operator price schedules reset during the window
position_start: Sudani bundle and call prices before the September 2025 increase
position_end: Prices raised by one operator in September 2025 and reset by the other in January 2026, with the current published schedule moved again since

subject: infra.connect
name: SIXP Sudan internet exchange point
milestone: Registry record last updated 22 January 2020
position_end: Four peers and a 4G aggregate capacity on the operator's own registry entry, with no membership change recorded since
note: Operated by the National Information Center; the entry is self-reported

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite internet — regulatory status
milestone: Services ordered cut at a West Kordofan locality from 26 August 2026
position_start: Unlicensed since SAF/TPRA import ban (Dec 2023); widely used via smuggled terminals; both SAF and RSF renting/confiscating regionally
position_end: Status contested and informal, with a new instance of localised enforcement: an armed group ordered every public market in a West Kordofan locality closed and satellite internet services cut off indefinitely from 26 August 2026, in a decision reported on 25 August 2026 by a local emergency room, which warned that severing satellite connectivity would cut displaced families off from relatives and from incoming remittances in a locality already under deteriorating security and living conditions; the order coincided with reinforcements arriving from Darfur
note: Never officially licensed in Sudan on any source held

subject: infra.connect
name: Sudatel terrestrial fibre backbone
milestone: 1,586 km of new backbone and 94 new sites added in 2025
position_end: Over 25,000 km of terrestrial fibre group-wide, with 1,586 km added and 94 new sites built in 2025, alongside stakes in the EASSy, SAS-1 and SAS-2 submarine systems

subject: infra.store
name: Khartoum State data centre (1,300 m2)
milestone: Restored and operational after technical rehabilitation; equipped for cloud computing, data security and AI-application hosting
position_start: Non-operational (date it went down not established)
position_end: Restored and operating, qualified to host government systems centrally
note: Distinct from Sudatel's separately-reported Khartoum data centre; that claim not corroborated in this pass

subject: infra.store
name: Port Sudan alternate National Data Centre
milestone: Announced as one of the digital ministry's future projects
position_end: Announced as planned; not built as of 2026-07-20
note: No construction start date given

subject: infra.store
name: Sudani core data centre, Port Sudan
milestone: Restored to full operation, reported 7 January 2026
position_start: Tier-4 data centre lost with the rest of the operator's Khartoum estate
position_end: Restored and fully operational from Port Sudan, serving government bodies, private institutions and citizens after losses the operator puts above USD 70 million
note: The group's FY2025 audit is qualified because war-related access restrictions prevented verification of property, plant and equipment

subject: infra.energy
name: National electricity grid
milestone: Assessed at August 2024
position_start: 3,500 MW installed capacity and a 32 per cent access rate before the war
position_end: 3,700 MW of pre-war installed capacity against a conflict-split, manually operated grid, isolated Darfur diesel grids without fuel, and up to USD 3 billion of war damage
note: No reliability indicators later than the 2019 diagnostic are held

subject: infra.energy
name: National policy linking digital infrastructure to energy supply
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-03 — an energy-and-digital-access operation is financed, but no policy instrument linking the two is held
position_end: Not held
note: No source on file; the Energy Ministry's grid-rehabilitation reporting names no digital-sector linkage

subject: infra.capacity
name: Compute or high-performance computing capacity
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-03 — the World Bank's country diagnostic reviews government ICT capacity without a compute specification, and no hosting contract beyond the two named data centres is held
position_end: Not held
note: No source on file

subject: infra.capacity
name: Sudan-CERT
milestone: Second training workshop of the year concluded 18 December 2025
position_end: Running domestic technical training for cybercrime prosecutors and police, twice in 2025

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Draft Cybersecurity Law
milestone: Redrafting with the digital transformation ministry reported 2026-08-11
position_end: No text published. After the Council of Ministers sent it back, the justice ministry states it is preparing the instrument in coordination with the digital transformation and communications ministry, as the Cybersecurity Regulation Law of 2026
note: Relationship to the cybercrime provisions Sudan separately described to the Tunis meeting (2026-07-30) is not established

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority
milestone: Established by PM decree alongside the Digital Transformation Authority and the Sudanese Data and AI Authority
position_end: Established; reports strict licensing standards and graduated sanctions to a Tunis Arab-experts forum
sources: 2025-11-07 Sudan Establishes Three Digital Authorities to Advance E-Govt|2026-07-30-suna-sudan-arab-experts-cybercrime-meeting-tunisia
note: Cybersecurity Tier 4 (48.17/100) cited alongside creation, 2025-11-07

subject: dpi.exchange
name: ASYCUDA customs system (Gezira/Hantoub)
milestone: Reactivated at Hantoub customs yard after war looting/damage, ahead of resuming formal customs operations
position_end: Reactivated at Hantoub only
sources: 2025-06-18 ASYCUDA customs system reactivated at Gezira state customs after war damage (SUNA)
note: Single pre-window source; no later report confirms further rollout to other customs stations

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Central bank electronic application system
milestone: Capital-flows system launched 2026-08-26
position_end: an electronic capital-flows system launched, replacing the manual processing it succeeds
note: no description of the system, its scope, its data or its completion date is given beyond the direction to finish it

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Electronic single window (National Investment Authority)
milestone: Authority says the window will operate electronically only once all investment-related entities are linked electronically; no list, sequence or date given
position_end: Precondition-stage; authority is also still building its first website
note: A single window is an interoperability commitment, not a portal; the two claims are not reconciled in the source

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National digital agricultural platform
milestone: Launch described as imminent, 2026-08-10
position_end: Developed by the agricultural bank with the agriculture and digital transformation ministries and described as expected to launch soon, alongside second-phase season financing opening by end-August 2026 and a grain-silo storage agreement signed with a Chinese company
note: no launch date, function, farmer register or data-protection basis is stated

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SEND shared cash transfer delivery platform
milestone: Technical specifications dated 15 December 2025
position_end: A shared payment and liquidity-management platform for the humanitarian cash consortium, specified against open government-to-person standards so it can interoperate with national social-protection systems over time

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Sudan Family Support Project management information system
milestone: Project closed; completion report issued 28 February 2025
position_end: A unified registration platform and payment infrastructure that reached 8.7 million people, sharing data with the national civil registry over an interface, suspended after the 2021 coup with its registries and payment rails reported still usable

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Sudanese Red Crescent 121 cash platform
milestone: Piloted in Red Sea and White Nile states
position_end: A live centralised system linking offline registration to automated deduplication and role-based access, piloted with 516 households in Red Sea State and 200 displaced people in White Nile at a full payment success rate

subject: dpi.id
name: Health and civil-registry electronic linkage
milestone: Joint higher committee agreed 16 March 2026
position_end: A joint higher committee and technical subcommittees agreed, with a new memorandum in preparation, to restore electronic linkage between the health and civil-registry systems from birth to death

subject: dpi.id
name: National number in bank-account opening
milestone: Central bank circular of 2 December 2024
position_end: Banks must record the national number and check it against the civil registry's own system when opening an account

subject: dpi.id
name: National root key for the public key infrastructure
milestone: Launched 12 March 2026
position_end: Launched as the trust anchor for electronic signatures and verification of digital documents and certificates

subject: dpi.id
name: SUDAPASS (national digital identity)
milestone: Banking-sector linkage begun, and its scope publicly bounded
position_start: Framed as imminent, with exclusion/surveillance-risk warnings
position_end: The communications and digital transformation ministry began linking the national digital identity to the banking sector, announced on 19 August 2026 with the central bank, the banking sector and the cyber security authority, so banks can verify customers and update records electronically without a branch visit, rolled out bank by bank as each becomes technically ready. On 23 August 2026 the central bank denied that registering for the identity exempts customers from updating their account data, saying claims circulating on social media had no basis in truth, that registration establishes identity only, and that its February 2026 directive requiring banks to update customer data still stands
sources: 2026-08-23-sudantribune-bank-of-sudan-sudapass-data-update|2026-08-19-sudantribune-sudapass-digital-bank-data-update-launch|2026-08-21-suna-sudan-baldna-trade-registry-integration|2026-08-20-sudan-sudapass-digital-id-banking-ekyc|2026-08-17-sudan-cbos-deadline-extension-sudapass|2026-05-21 Sudan launches national digital identity SUDAPASS (SUNA)|2026-02-02 Sudan's planned national digital ID could strengthen recovery push - Experts|2026-01-29 How to build trust alongside Sudan's digital identity system
note: no enrolment count is held, and tying bank-account continuity to a credential whose coverage is unmeasured is the exclusion risk the base recorded before launch - the integration announced by the digital transformation ministry and the central bank on 2026-08-20 is that risk being realised rather than answered, because the eKYC route makes the credential the condition of keeping an account current in a country where displacement is mass and the coverage figure is still unpublished

subject: dpi.pay
name: Al-Asjad payment-switch licence
milestone: Central Bank revoked the licence days after the platform's launch; no specific breach disclosed
position_start: Licensed, launched in Port Sudan with a Sovereignty Council representative present
position_end: Licence revoked; unconfirmed press reports the firm was incorporated only in late 2025 with a Dubai branch
note: UAE linkage reported by Sudanese outlets, not confirmed by the Central Bank

subject: dpi.pay
name: Bankak (Bank of Khartoum mobile money)
milestone: Reported as dominant retail-settlement rail in Khartoum markets, driven by cash scarcity and currency collapse, not technology uptake
movement: No change, qualifying clause: national payment switch launched with one other bank as a nascent counterweight, not yet material
position_start: Single-provider concentration already flagged as a vulnerability (2025-03)
position_end: Still dominant; recurring failure modes (no-smartphone workarounds, app outages, mistaken transfers) documented from field reporting
note: A separate war-economy analysis (2026-07-24) finds Bankak volumes now a monetary mass outside central-bank supervision

subject: dpi.pay
name: Bede digital wallet (Zain)
milestone: Launched in Port Sudan; phase 1 covers transfers, airtime, bill payments, merchant purchases, agent cash in/out
position_end: Phase 1 live
sources: 2025-04-18 Zain Launches Bede Digital Wallet to Boost Financial Inclusion in Sudan
note: Single source predates the 12-month comparison window; no later report confirms progression to phases 2/3

subject: dpi.pay
name: Enforcement against unlicensed payment applications
milestone: A licence revoked 4 July 2026 and a public alert issued 28 January 2026
position_end: A public alert against an unlicensed financial application operating in areas held by the Rapid Support Forces, and an electronic-payment licence revoked after a technical and legal review

subject: dpi.pay
name: Isali / Eisali (electronic government-collection system)
milestone: Named among the reforms behind a stated rise in first-half 2026 revenue
position_end: National Workers Bank contracted (2026-04-30); diffused Gadarif to Kassala (2026-05-03); White Nile self-reports over 90% of transactions electronic, unverified; named as the platform authorities are to link to, and on 2026-08-10 named by the finance ministry - with electronic invoicing and tightened customs and tax exemptions - as the means by which first-half 2026 public revenue rose significantly without new taxes
sources: 2026-08-10-sudan-finance-ministry-reform-package-revenue|2026-08-04-sudan-finance-minister-digital-transformation-directives|2026-04-30 Finance Ministry-National Workers Bank contract for Isali e-collection service (SUNA)|2026-05-03 Gadarif transfers Isali electronic-collection experience to Kassala state (SUNA)|2026-07-30-suna-minister-of-finance-praises-white-nile-electronic-collection
note: White Nile's >90% figure is the state's own, unverified; the ministry states no revenue figure, baseline or attribution method behind the claimed rise

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Instant Payment System / national payment switch (NIPS)
milestone: Launched live, connecting Omdurman National Bank as first and only participant; first ATM withdrawal completed over the switch
position_start: Public tender open for a software-only solution (2026-04-20); by 2026-07-08 contracted to Electronic Banking Services (EBS) but not launched
position_end: Live with exactly one bank connected; explicitly framed by the central bank as restoration of war-damaged infrastructure, not a new build; no schedule for connecting remaining banks
note: Central Bank's own framing is restoration, not a greenfield rail

subject: dpi.pay
name: Saudi Sudanese Bank card-processing agreement
milestone: Signed 19 January 2026
position_end: End-to-end digital payment processing, Mastercard sponsorship and prepaid-card issuing contracted with an external processor; not itself a live cross-border rail

subject: dpi.pay
name: SWIFT service bureau accreditation
milestone: Accredited, announced 11 June 2026
position_end: The central bank's payments arm accredited as a SWIFT service bureau, an enabling step towards connecting the banking sector to international messaging standards

subject: dpi.pay
name: USSD banking service
milestone: Rolled out jointly by the digital ministry, Central Bank and telecoms regulator; works without internet access
position_end: Phase 1 covers interpersonal transfers, credit inquiries, transaction summaries
sources: 2026-03-18 Sudan Launches USSD Banking Services to Expand Digital Financial Access
note: Operational details for participating banks/telcos were to be announced separately; none held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Zakher wallet
milestone: Recurring-debit interface launched 24 August 2026
position_end: Carrying a new interface for pre-authorised recurring deductions, offered as an alternative to cheques for subscriptions, instalments, rent, government fees and business collections

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil Registry Act 2011
milestone: Repealed and replaced the 2001 Act
position_end: In force, founding the national civil registry and its unique national number, and requiring the registry to supply data to competent state organs

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registry population coverage
milestone: Reported by Sudanese authorities for 2021
movement: No change, a figure the base has not held since
position_start: 82 per cent registered, on the official figure reported for 2016
position_end: 35.5 million of 40 million inhabitants, about 88.8 per cent, registered by 2021, with coverage materially lower in peripheral and displaced populations
note: No national coverage figure has been published since the war began

subject: dpi.registry
name: General Commercial Register
milestone: Administrative work in Port Sudan suspended from 14 December 2025
position_start: A computerised company database built from 2003 across 13 state branch offices
position_end: Operating from a computerised database built from 2003, with all administrative work in Port Sudan including the trademark office suspended from 14 December 2025 and no resumption date given
note: The registrar's own description still cites the 1925 Companies Act rather than the 2015 Act

subject: dpi.registry
name: General Electoral Register
milestone: Established by the National Elections Act 2008
position_end: The operative but dormant legal framework: no evidence of an operational register after 2023 was found, and no elections have been held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land Registries Administration
status: Implemented, recovering under a transfer freeze
milestone: Jabal Awliya office reopened, 2 April 2026
position_start: Offices burned and reverted to paper registers, with electronic linkage lost
position_end: 106 branch offices under a central registrar, with the electronic system being restored, the Jabal Awliya office reopened, and a six-month freeze on sales and transfers over parcels whose registers had just been reconstituted
note: Land registration has sat with the judiciary since 1909, under the Land Settlement and Registration Act 1925

subject: dpi.registry
name: National postal addressing system
milestone: A statutory mandate under the Telecommunications and Post (Organization) Act 2018
position_end: Provided for as a regulator's statutory duty to establish and manage a postal addressing system; no deployed national register is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register
milestone: Tax-base expansion initiative launched, reported 23 July 2026
position_start: A register operating on mandatory 30-day registration and a single tax identification number
position_end: Operating on a single tax identification number covering all tax types including customs, with monthly data sharing from the commercial register, and an initiative launched to close a gap the IMF estimates leaves over 60 per cent of economic activity outside the net

subject: dpi.registry
name: Unified Social Registry
milestone: Ministers reviewed progress on a foundational social-protection targeting database
position_end: In development; no completion date, coverage or data source given
sources: 2026-04-19 Ministerial meeting on digital transformation, civil-service reform and unified social registry (SUNA)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Vehicle registration database (traffic police)
milestone: Restored register: 2,124,750 registered vehicles, 3,161,599 driving licences; backup data centres built inside the states and abroad
position_end: 2,124,750 vehicles, 3,161,599 licences; Salem e-renewal serving 16 countries (up from six); Ansab laser-secured ownership-transfer platform being introduced
note: Offsite/in-state backup credited with the registry's survival through the war

subject: dpi.mis
name: Afia (health-sector platform)
milestone: Digital ministry, Health Ministry and WHO met to set a comprehensive health-digital strategy; Afia referenced, WHO urging acceleration
position_end: Referenced as forthcoming, no launch date given
